2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.1.title: Identifying a duplicate charge
2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.1.text: A duplicate charge exists when two or more POSTED purchases share the same merchant and amount within 24 hours and have different authorization codes. Repeat purchases with different amounts are not duplicates.

2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.2.title: Provisional credit for duplicates
2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.2.text: When a duplicate is confirmed, issue provisional credit equal to the duplicated amount immediately if the amount is 500 USD or less. Above 500 USD, supervisor approval is required before credit is issued.

2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.3.title: Pending authorization holds
2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.3.text: If one entry is PENDING and shares the authorization code with a POSTED entry, it is an authorization hold and not a duplicate. Do not issue credit. Tell the customer the hold drops off automatically within 7 business days.

2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.4.title: Raising the dispute
2026-01:SOP-DISP-4.4.text: If the customer asks to dispute a confirmed duplicate, raise a dispute with reason code 12.6.1 (Duplicate Processing) and attach both transaction ids. Confirm the customer has not received a refund from the merchant.

2026-01:SOP-REF-3.1.title: Refund posting timeline
2026-01:SOP-REF-3.1.text: Merchant refunds post to the card within 10 business days after the merchant issues them. If the refund was issued less than 10 business days ago, no dispute can be raised; tell the customer the expected posting date.

2026-01:SOP-REF-3.2.title: Overdue refunds
2026-01:SOP-REF-3.2.text: If more than 10 business days have passed since the merchant issued the refund and no matching REFUND appears, raise a chargeback with reason code 13.6 (Credit Not Processed). Provisional credit may be issued only after the chargeback is raised.

2026-01:SOP-REF-3.3.title: Required documents
2026-01:SOP-REF-3.3.text: For a chargeback the customer must provide the merchant's refund confirmation or return receipt. If the customer has no proof, advise them to request it from the merchant before filing.

2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.1.title: Fraud indicators
2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.1.text: Count these indicators: transaction country differs from the customer's usual country; online or card-not-present channel; transaction between 01:00 and 05:00 local time; first-time merchant; two or more charges at the same merchant within 24 hours; amount at least 5 times the customer's average purchase.

2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.2.title: Immediate actions
2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.2.text: With two or more indicators and the customer confirming the card is in their possession, block the card immediately, order a replacement card, open a fraud case, and issue provisional credit for the disputed amounts within 1 business day.

2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.3.title: When not to auto-credit
2026-01:SOP-FRD-5.3.text: With fewer than two indicators, or if the customer mentions a family member, a shared device or a known merchant, do not issue credit. Route the case to manual review by the fraud team.

2026-01:SOP-REC-6.1.title: Proof of cancellation
2026-01:SOP-REC-6.1.text: A recurring charge posted after the customer's cancellation date is disputable only if the customer can state the cancellation date and provide a cancellation confirmation. Without a stated cancellation date, route to manual review.

2026-01:SOP-REC-6.2.title: Provisional credit
2026-01:SOP-REC-6.2.text: Issue provisional credit for charges posted after the cancellation date, up to 2 billing cycles. For more than 2 cycles, supervisor approval is required.

2026-01:SOP-REC-6.3.title: Dispute and stop payment
2026-01:SOP-REC-6.3.text: Raise a dispute with reason code 13.2 (Cancelled Recurring Transaction) and place a recurring-payment stop on the merchant to block future charges.
